title: GRACE designs two carbonic-anhydrase-like enzymes with measured catalytic activity
summary: The GRACE workflow combined RFdiffusion structure generation, ProteinMPNN sequence design, CLEAN enzyme classification and solubility/structure filtering to select two carbonic-anhydrase-like sequences from 10,000 candidates. The authors report experimental expression and carbonic anhydrase activity: dCA12_2 at 400 WAU/mL and dCA23_1 at 260 WAU/mL in the reported assay.
ai_technology: GRACE (RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and CLEAN, with computational solubility/structural filters)
organization: National Cheng Kung University and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: The authors report experimental expression and carbonic anhydrase activity: dCA12_2 at 400 WAU/mL and dCA23_1 at 260 WAU/mL in the reported assay.
evidence.unknown: The reported activity values are from the study's carbonic-anhydrase assay and do not establish purified-enzyme kinetics, physiological CO2-fixation performance, or industrial utility. The designs and validation are a two-protein proof of concept; no independent replication assessed.
evidence.ai_role: The generative-design workflow produced structures/sequences and machine-learning function classification prioritized two candidates from a 10,000-sequence pool; researchers expressed both and measured carbonic-anhydrase activity.
